summary: The lecture surveys modern security architectures, contrasting traditional access‑control mechanisms (ACLs, capabilities, RBAC) with newer Zero‑Trust and micro‑segmentation approaches. It then explores privacy‑preserving techniques, blockchain‑based ledgers, and AI‑driven behavioral analytics, before covering OS hardening mechanisms such as ASLR, RELRO, and covert‑channel defenses.
title: Modern Security Architectures and Privacy‑Preserving Techniques

topics.title: Traditional Access‑Control Models and Least‑Privilege Principles
Zero‑Trust Architecture, Micro‑Segmentation, and Centralized Logging
Blockchain, Distributed Ledgers, and Smart Contracts
Behavioral Analytics and Machine‑Learning‑Based Threat Detection
Advanced OS Hardening and Covert‑Channel Defenses

fun_fact_idea.exciting_angle: Show how the same ML techniques that power behavioral analytics can be the core of a startup offering AI‑driven zero‑trust monitoring as a SaaS, turning security data into a revenue‑generating product for cloud customers.
search_queries: CrowdStrike machine learning security monitoring case study
Darktrace AI anomaly detection enterprise security blog
fun_fact_idea.search_reasoning: Concrete examples from leading security‑AI companies will illustrate how the lecture’s concepts translate into real‑world SaaS products, making the connection vivid for an aspiring AI‑focused software‑engineer entrepreneur.
